_meta.what_this_is: A simple learner simulation to compare item-difficulty policies. The learner has a skill level; an item has a difficulty; the chance of solving it is the logistic of (skill - difficulty). The learning signal from an item is largest when the outcome is most uncertain -- when success probability is near one half -- and near zero when the item is trivially easy or hopelessly hard. Three policies pick item difficulty relative to the learner CURRENT skill: too_easy stays well below it, too_hard well above it, targeted sits right at it (even odds).
_meta.data_is: A FIXTURE. The policy offsets, learning rate, item count, and starting skill are hand-chosen so the targeted policy reaches skill 3.000 while the too-easy and too-hard policies both stall at 0.841 -- the symmetry showing both extremes waste the item equally. Every skill trajectory and gain is computed in difficulty.py.
_meta.format: policies: {name: difficulty_offset from current skill}; start_skill; items; learning_rate.
